Campaign proposition: European Expert Evals for Multilingual AI
Priority account cluster: Mistral AI; DeepL; ElevenLabs; Cohere; Aleph Alpha
Commercial trigger: New multilingual, voice and document models are moving into enterprise workflows where generic benchmarks miss professional and cultural nuance.
Buyer committee: Head of Evals; Research Partnerships; Enterprise Product; Safety/Trust; Applied AI
Buyer problem: Internal teams can measure benchmark performance, but may lack verified domain experts, language coverage and independent adjudication for difficult real-world tasks.
Partnership wedge: Verified European academics and professionals design hard tasks, adjudicate failures and document why a model fails—across relevant languages and regulated domains.
Illustrative two-week entry offer: One domain × two languages: expert-authored task set, evaluation rubric, blinded model review, failure taxonomy and an evidence pack. Scope and volumes are illustrative, not a Sovrano commitment.
Evidence of success: Agreed rubric coverage; inter-reviewer agreement; useful failure categories; decision-ready findings; documented provenance and delivery against the agreed schedule.
Expansion route: More languages and domains; release regression suites; customer-specific benchmarks; safety/red-team programmes; recurring evaluation retainer.
Primary CTA: Would a 20-minute scope test reveal a language/domain gap your current eval stack does not cover?
Publication boundary: Public: proposition, method and 2–3 sample accounts. Private: full target list, people mapping and prioritisation notes.

Campaign proposition: Expert Task Intelligence for Physical AI
Priority account cluster: 1X; Agile Robots; Apptronik; NEURA Robotics; Physical Intelligence
Commercial trigger: Embodied-AI teams are scaling human video, robot demonstrations, simulation and on-policy data, but task quality and evaluation still depend on precise human expertise.
Buyer committee: Head of Robot Learning; Data/World Models; Evaluation; Fleet Operations; Research Partnerships
Buyer problem: Collecting more generic data can reproduce weak task definitions. Specialist workflows require experts who know the correct sequence, edge cases, safety boundaries and what successful performance looks like.
Partnership wedge: European operators and domain professionals create task specifications, coached demonstrations and independent failure adjudication—with consent, provenance and a staged delivery model.
Illustrative two-week entry offer: Desktop-first pilot: decompose one specialist workflow into task steps, edge cases, acceptance rubric and capture specification; progress to demonstrations only after hardware, rights and safety requirements are agreed.
Evidence of success: Task coverage; expert acceptance of the rubric; actionable failure modes; capture feasibility; documented rights/provenance; clear go/no-go criteria for physical data collection.
Expansion route: Additional task families and environments; demonstration cohorts; policy evaluation; deployment QA; ongoing expert review of on-policy data.
Primary CTA: Before investing in another data batch, would it be useful to test whether the task and acceptance criteria are defined tightly enough?
Publication boundary: Public: method and sample hypothesis. Private: operational requirements, access route and any people/contact research.

Priority account cluster: BBVA; BNP Paribas; Santander; Allianz; Zurich; AXA
Commercial trigger: Banks and insurers are moving GenAI and agentic systems into customer, claims, underwriting, KYC and internal workflows while governance expectations intensify.
Buyer committee: Group AI/Transformation; Model Risk; Compliance/Legal; Business Owner; Responsible AI; Procurement
Buyer problem: The builder, primary vendor and internal owner may all be invested in the system. Leaders still need independent, domain-expert evidence about accuracy, escalation, bias, explanations and operational risk.
Partnership wedge: A fixed-scope independent evaluation using professional experts, synthetic or authorised cases, traceable rubrics and a decision-ready evidence report.
Illustrative two-week entry offer: One workflow × up to two languages: risk-based test design, synthetic-case evaluation, human adjudication, failure taxonomy and executive findings. It is evaluation evidence—not legal certification.
Evidence of success: Coverage of priority risks; evidence quality; consistency of adjudication; actionable remediation; executive usability; documented limitations and provenance.
Expansion route: More countries and workflows; release gates; vendor/model comparisons; recurring regression tests; independent governance and evaluation retainer.
Primary CTA: Could one fixed-price independent evaluation strengthen the next release or governance decision without exposing production data?
Publication boundary: Public: method, synthetic examples and selected public signals. Private: specific opportunity mapping, people and commercial assumptions.
